newsitem.title: CHINA: China Shipping, Singapore in pact.
newsitem.headline: China Shipping, Singapore in pact.

text.p: China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO) on Monday signed a deal with the Port of Singapore that gives China's national shipping firm stable prices in return for making the port a hub for container operations.

Under the long-term agreement, the port will promise COSCO stable long-term prices and service while the company pledges to increase its container operations there, port spokeswoman Dawn Wong told reporters after a signing ceremony in Beijing.
Wong declined to detail terms of the deal, such as prices and the timetable, but said the agreement was for between three and 10 years.
COSCO has listed units in Singapore, COSCO Investment (Singapore) Ltd, and Hong Kong, COSCO Pacific Ltd.

COSCO's container business with the Port of Singapore had grown rapidly since the two sides signed a container deal in 1994, and the firm now had about 60 container ships docked at the port at any given time, said Chen Zhongbiao, president of COSCO.
"I am confident that the growth will continue at an even more rapid pace under the new agreement," said Khoo Teng Chye, president of the Port of Singapore Authority Group.
COSCO and the port were looking at other cooperative ventures in region, Khoo said, but gave no further details.
The deal was part of Singapore's efforts to boost competitiveness with other regional ports such as those in Malaysia and Thailand, Wong said.
